extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current patent and trademark practitioners, inventors seeking counsel, law students, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and administrative responsibilities governing who may represent parties before the USPTO in patent and trademark matters, including practitioner eligibility, oversight, and related programs (e.g., pro bono and clinic certification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent practitioner registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent practitioners are individuals who have passed the USPTO's registration exam and met the qualifications to represent patent applicants before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) administers the registration exam and maintains a roster of current patent practitioners. See 'Becoming a patent practitioner' for requirements, forms, and exam information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark practitioner eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark practitioners are attorneys who are active members in good standing of the bar of the highest court of any State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Becoming a trademark practitioner' for more information and 'Finding a trademark practitioner' to locate attorneys who practice trademark law.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED responsibilities (administration and oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) administers the registration exam and maintains a roster of current patent practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond exam administration, OED coordinates oversight functions described on the page (see also discipline, pro bono, and clinic programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and disciplinary oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: OED investigates grievances submitted against practitioners and provides public information about disciplinary actions against practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners are subject to ethics rules and potential disciplinary processes; see 'Information for current patent practitioners' which lists ethics rules, common forms, and online access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono Program coordination and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: OED coordinates a nationwide Patent Pro Bono Program for under-resourced inventors seeking free legal help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program targets under-resourced inventors in need of pro bono assistance; practitioners and volunteers can participate through the coordinated program (see the program page for eligibility and participation details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Law School Clinic Certification Program
rubrics_metrics.description: OED administers a Law School Clinic Certification Program where law students gain experience in intellectual property law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified law school clinics permit law students, under supervision, to gain practice experience in IP matters; program administration and certification criteria are handled by OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to practice before the USPTO (verification / finding practitioners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find registered patent agents and attorneys who are eligible to practice before the USPTO in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those who meet USPTO registration/eligibility requirements (e.g., registration exam passage for patent practitioners) are eligible; the USPTO provides resources to locate and verify practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for current practitioners (compliance and administration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find useful information for current patent practitioners including ethics rules, common forms, and online access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current practitioners should consult these resources to comply with USPTO rules, complete administrative tasks, and access online practitioner services.
